_doc: WireGuard hub endpoint declarations for the Surface Pro NixOS host. Mirrors the schema of cloud/config.json#native.wireguard. The 'fallback' endpoint is the hub-side NAT redirect (Phase 4: udp/<fallback.port> -> udp/<primary.port> on gcp-proxy via firewall.nix). Use the wg-fallback helper to switch when the primary port is blocked (airports/hotels).
_ipv6_doc: wg0 dual-stack fields (2026-07-26). The cloud fleet's wg0 mesh became dual-stack — verified in cloud/config.json (wireguard.subnet_v6 = fd0c:1d00::/64; peers[] each carry wg_ipv6, including surface = fd0c:1d00::5). client.wg_ipv6/subnet_v6 mirror that data so this host's NM profile can add ipv6.method=manual instead of ignore.

fallback._doc: Hub-side NAT redirect on gcp-proxy (deployed Phase 4 via firewall.nix). Use when networks block udp/51820.

_mtu_doc: Tunnel MTU. 1280, not WireGuard's usual 1420, because this tunnel must survive riding INSIDE a CLAT/NAT64 path. PROVEN IN THE FIELD 2026-08-12: on a v6-only WiFi the clat default route carries `mtu 1260`, so a 1420-byte wg frame plus ~60 bytes of outer IPv4+UDP+WireGuard header exceeds it and is dropped with DF set. Normally Path MTU Discovery would correct that — but ICMP on this path is filtered at EVERY size (verified: `ping -M do -s 100` through 1400 to 1.1.1.1, all dropped), so PMTUD is a BLACK HOLE. The failure is vicious precisely because it is partial: small packets pass, so TCP connects and the port reads as open, and only the first large frame dies. SSH to 10.0.0.4 completed its TCP handshake and then hung at SSH2_MSG_KEX_ECDH_REPLY — the key exchange is the first big packet — which reads like an auth or host-key fault and is not one.
_mtu_conflict_doc: UNRESOLVED TENSION ON CLAT PATHS — READ BEFORE CHANGING THIS VALUE. On the specific v6-only WiFi encountered 2026-08-12 the clat route MTU is 1260, so the outer wg frame must stay under it: inner <= ~1200. But IPv6 requires inner >= 1280. Those two constraints have NO overlap, so on that network you must pick which one breaks. Measured, with everything else held constant: mtu 1200 -> mesh HTTPS works (mcp.diegonmarcos.com returns 200) but wg0 has NO IPv6 at all and NM therefore drops dns-search on the next activation; mtu 1280 -> IPv6 and all three routing domains are correct but mesh HTTPS fails with 'Error in the HTTP2 framing layer'. TCP MSS clamping was tried as the standard escape and DID NOT HELP: with an nftables rule (output, oifname wg0, syn, maxseg 1140) held in place across both, 1200 still returned 200 and 1280 still failed — so the limit is not TCP segment size and the mechanism is not fully explained. advmss on the wg0 routes did not help either. 1280 is kept as the committed value because it is the RFC8200 floor, it is correct on any ordinary network (path 1500, where nothing conflicts), and the alternative silently breaks IPv6 and DNS. The degradation is a property of that one broken WiFi, not of this configuration. If you are ON such a network, lower it TEMPORARILY and by hand — and expect to re-push routing domains with `resolvectl domain wg0 ~diegonmarcos.com ~app ~db` afterwards.
_mtu_floor_doc: 1280 IS A HARD FLOOR, NOT A TUNING CHOICE — do not lower it. 1280 is the minimum MTU IPv6 permits (RFC8200). Set this interface below it and the kernel DISABLES IPv6 on the device and drops every v6 address, including the link-local. That is not cosmetic here: without a link-local, NetworkManager's IPv6 stage can never complete, and because it never completes NM never commits the link's finished IP configuration to systemd-resolved — so ipv6.dns AND dns-search are silently dropped, `~diegonmarcos.com` stops routing to Hickory, mesh names resolve to public IPs, and every `wg_only: true` route starts answering 403. Learned the hard way the same day: 1200 was tried first (1260 - 20 IPv4 - 8 UDP - 32 WireGuard, sized to fit the clat path exactly), it fixed the ssh hang, and it silently re-broke IPv6 and DNS by exactly the mechanism configuration_network.nix's addr-gen-mode note describes. 1280 was then verified to satisfy BOTH constraints at once: ssh to 10.0.0.4 succeeds, wg0 keeps fd0c:1d00::5/64 + fe80::…, and resolved keeps all three routing domains.
_mtu_resolution_doc: TENSION RESOLVED 2026-08-19 — mtu lowered 1280 -> 1200. The blocker for 1200 was never the RFC8200 floor itself but its side effect: no IPv6 on wg0 means NetworkManager drops ipv4.dns-search on the next activation, so mcp.diegonmarcos.com stopped resolving to Hickory. That is now compensated declaratively: ba_flakes_desktop/src/modules/cloud-network-wg-dns.json carries the full routing-domain list and wg-dns-up.sh re-pushes it with resolvectl on every wg0 up, independent of NM and of IPv6. Cost of 1200: wg0 carries no IPv6 (fd0c:1d00::5/64 is not assigned); the mesh is IPv4-only (10.0.0.0/24) so nothing routes over it today. Benefit: TLS handshakes to the mesh edge stop blackholing on clat/tethered paths (curl to mcp.diegonmarcos.com went from a 20.9s reset to code=200, tls=0.963s). Restore 1280 only together with a wg0 IPv6 consumer.
_dns_search_doc: systemd-resolved routing domains (~ prefix) sent to Hickory (hub.wg_ip). Mirrors the zones Hickory serves: cloud/a_solutions/infra-net_hickory-dns/build.json .dns.zones = [diegonmarcos.com, app, db]. Without a zone here, its names fall through to the global resolver (dnscrypt-proxy2) and NXDOMAIN. MUST be a JSON array — one routing domain per element. configuration_network.nix joins these with ';' for NetworkManager's ipv4.dns-search keyfile list. A single space-joined string is mis-parsed by NM as ONE domain literally named 'diegonmarcos.com ~app ~db', so mcp.diegonmarcos.com never routed to Hickory → public IP → Caddy WG-gate 403.
_hickory_ipv6_doc: Hickory DNS also listens over IPv6 on the mesh (cloud/a_solutions/infra-net_hickory-dns/src/flake.nix — bind :: on port 53, reachable at fd0c:1d00::1, same host as hub.wg_ip). Added alongside ipv4.dns=hub.wg_ip in the wg0 NM profile so mesh split-DNS keeps working once wg0 carries an IPv6 address.
_tunnel_mode_doc: split | full. split = only subnet + subnet_v6 are routed into the tunnel (mesh-only; the rest of your traffic uses the local WiFi/LTE). full = 0.0.0.0/0 + ::/0 are routed into the tunnel (all traffic exits via the hub). Read by configuration_network.nix, which derives BOTH the peer allowed-ips AND ipv4/ipv6.never-default AND the dispatcher-script wg set from this one field — never edit those three by hand or they will disagree. Only ONE interface may be full at a time: two default routes over two wg devices fight.
